title: Diagnose and recover a stale PostgreSQL idle transaction
trigger: A PostgreSQL transaction exceeds the approved age threshold or monitoring reports a session remaining idle in transaction beyond the service baseline.
preconditions: identify the exact application/session context rather than acting on age alone
capture pg_stat_activity including state, xact_start, query_start, wait event, and last query
capture relevant pg_locks evidence before terminating a backend
confirm whether customer sessions are currently blocked or whether this is proactive transaction-risk remediation
obtain the required simulated approval for backend termination
diagnostic_steps: query pg_stat_activity for sessions with state idle in transaction
compare transaction age against the operational threshold
capture locks held by the target backend
check for lock-waiting sessions separately so lock contention is not assumed
check recent release/change context when available
mitigation_steps: terminate only the single approved backend that matches the captured application identity, idle-in-transaction state, and age threshold
do not restart PostgreSQL to clear one stale transaction
do not mass-terminate sessions solely because their age exceeds a threshold
validation_steps: the targeted application session is no longer present in pg_stat_activity
an independent write to the affected data path succeeds within the expected lock timeout
no unexpected new lock waiter appears after recovery
escalation_boundary: Escalate to DBA/application ownership when the session is business-critical, ownership cannot be confirmed, termination risk is unclear, the transaction repeatedly reappears, replication/maintenance impact is suspected, or application behavior must be changed to prevent recurrence.
